net sales.text: Our revenue is derived from three main sources: (a) products, (b) service and subscription, and (c) royalties. net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text: Our revenue is derived from three main sources: (a) products, (b) service and subscription, and (c) royalties. Our performance obligations are satisfied at a point in time or over time as stand ready obligations. Product revenue is recognized at the point in time when the customer takes control of the product, which typically occurs at the point of shipment. Service and subscription revenue consists of customer support agreements, software subscriptions, installation, and consulting & training. Our software subscriptions include term licenses which are recognized as revenue when the license has been delivered to the customer and related customer support which is recognized ratably over the service period. Revenue from customer support agreements is recognized ratably over the contractual term of the agreement. Installation services are typically completed within a short period of time and revenue from these services are recognized at the point when installation is complete. A majority of our consulting and training revenue does not take significant time to complete therefore these obligations are satisfied upon completion of such services over time as each day is completed. We license certain products under royalty arrangements, pursuant to which our licensees periodically provide us with reports containing units sold to end users subject to the royalties.

lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

During the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, one customer represented more than 10% of our total revenue and during the fiscal year ended March 31, 2025, no customer represented 10% or more of our total revenue.
In fiscal 2026, one customer represented more than 10% of total revenues and in fiscal 2025 no customer represented more than 10% of the Company's total revenue.
Accordingly, you should not rely on forward-looking statements as predictions of future events.
• Cost increases, supply disruptions, or raw material shortages, including in single source components, could harm our business.
Quantum's tape storage systems are designed by Quantum and manufactured by a global contract manufacturer.
We generally rely on patent, copyright, trademark and trade secret laws and contract rights to establish and maintain our proprietary rights in our technology and products.
We currently rely on a single contract manufacturer to manufacture our products and to provide warehousing and logistics services for our spare parts.

In many cases, our business partners are the sole source of supply for the products or parts they manufacture, or the services they provide to us, and we do not have executed long-term purchase agreements with these partners.
We rely on indirect sales channels to market and sell our branded products.
Our future operating results may depend upon the continued service of our key personnel and in significant part upon our ability to attract and retain qualified management personnel.

Our operating results depend on continuing and increasing market acceptance of our existing products and on new product introductions, which may be unsuccessful, in which case our business, financial condition and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected.

A limited number of products comprise a significant majority of our sales, and due to rapid technological change in our industry, our future operating results depend on our ability to improve existing products and develop and successfully introduce new products.
We rely on a combination of copyright, patent, trademark, and trade secrets laws and nondisclosure agreements to establish and protect our proprietary technology.

Any determination to pay dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our Board of Directors, and will depend on our financial condition, operating results, capital requirements, general business conditions and other factors that our Board may deem relevant.
As a result, capital appreciation, if any, of our common stock will be the sole source of gain for the foreseeable future.

Due to our history of net losses in the U.S., the protracted period for utilizing tax attributes in certain foreign jurisdictions, and the difficulty in predicting future results, we believe that we cannot rely on projections of future taxable income to realize most of our deferred tax assets.

Our principal sources of liquidity include cash from operating activities, cash and cash equivalents on our balance sheet and proceeds from the sale of Common Stock under the SEPA (as defined herein).
Our future liquidity requirements will depend on multiple factors, including our research and development plans and capital asset needs.
Our revenue is derived from three main sources: (a) products, (b) service and subscription, and (c) royalties.
The Company generates revenue from three main sources: (1) product, (2) service and subscription, and (3) royalties.
In many cases, the Company’s chosen vendor may be the sole source of supply for the products or parts they manufacture, or services they provide, for the Company.
Some of the products the Company purchases from these sources are proprietary or complex in nature, and therefore cannot be readily or easily replaced by alternative sources.
Sales of common stock under the SEPA may be made by the Company at its discretion from time to time and will depend upon market conditions and other factors.

The amount of additional capital that may be raised under the SEPA will depend on market conditions, trading volumes, the Company’s stock price, and the continued satisfaction of the applicable limitations and conditions under the agreement.
Due to its history of net losses and the difficulty in predicting future results, Quantum believes that it cannot rely on projections of future taxable income to realize the deferred tax assets.
Because the valuation relies on significant unobservable inputs, the fair value of the Forbearance Warrant is classified as Level 3 within the fair value hierarchy.

The Company estimated the fair value of the Convertible Note using a Monte Carlo simulation method, as the Convertible Note includes features for which the settlement outcome depends on the path of the Company’s common stock price and other variables over time.
